'''David Michael Patrick Mingos''' (born 6 August 1944) is a British [[chemist]] and academic. He was Principal of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]] from 1999 to 2009, and Professor of [[Inorganic Chemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oxford University Gazette: Recognition of Distinction 1999-2000 (supplement) |url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/2000-1/supps/2_4558.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224222858/https://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/2000-1/supps/2_4558.htm |archive-date=2018-02-24 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ox.ac.uk/publicaffairs/pubs/annualreview/ar99/heads.shtml University of Oxford Annual Review 1998/99] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070705154929/http://www.ox.ac.uk/publicaffairs/pubs/annualreview/ar99/heads.shtml |date=5 July 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Full History of the Hall |url=https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/about-college/full-history-hall |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714045647/https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/about-college/full-history-hall |archive-date=2018-07-14 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=St Edmund Hall |language=en}}</ref><ref>[http://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/sites/default/files/1269350393_Mingos__Mike_updated_CV_Mar_2010.pdf Michael Mingos's CV]</ref><ref>
''Debrett's People of Today'' (12th edn, London: Debrett's Peerage, 1999), p.&nbsp;1362</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Michael Mingos, FRS Authorised Biography – Debrett’s People of Today, Prof Michael Mingos, FRS Profile |url=http://www.debretts.com/people/people-of-today/people-of-today-search-results.aspx?personId=4163&name=(David)%20Michael%20Patrick+MINGOS |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130710005934/http://www.debretts.com/people/people-of-today/people-of-today-search-results.aspx?personId=4163&name=(David)%20Michael%20Patrick+MINGOS |archive-date=2013-07-10 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.debretts.com}}</ref>

==Education==
Mingos attended the [[Harvey Grammar School]], [[King Edward VII and Queen Mary School|King Edward VII School Lytham St Anne's]], [[University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology]] (Chemistry Department Prize 1963, [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] First Class 1965, [[Doctor of Science|Hon DSc]] 2000), and the [[University of Sussex]] ([[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] 1968,<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Sussex|title=The preparation and properties of some tertiary phosphine complexes of osmium, iridium, ruthenium, and platinum.|first= David Michael Patrick|last=Mingos|year=1968|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.465790|oclc=500519525}}</ref> and [[Doctor of Science|Hon DSc]] 2001).

==Career==
Mingos undertook [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Northwestern University]] ([[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellow]] 1968–70) and at the [[University of Sussex]] ([[Imperial Chemical Industries|ICI Fellow]] 1970–71). From 1971 until 1976 he was a Lecturer at [[Queen Mary, University of London]]. He then moved to the University of Oxford as [[Fellow#Oxford, Cambridge and Dublin|Fellow and Tutor]] at [[Keble College, Oxford|Keble College]] and University Lecturer. From 1977 until 1992 he was also Lecturer at [[Pembroke College, Oxford]].

In 1978, Mingos, [[Stephen G. Davies]] and [[Malcolm Green (chemist)|Malcolm Green]] compiled a [[Green–Davies–Mingos rules|set of rules]] that summarise where [[Addition to pi ligands|nucleophilic additions]] will occur on pi ligands.<ref>{{cite journal| doi=10.1016/0040-4020(78)87001-X | volume=34 | issue=20 | title=Nucleophilic addition to organotransition metal cations containing unsaturated hydrocarbon ligands | year=1978 | journal=Tetrahedron | pages=3047–3077 | last1 = Davies | first1 = Stephen G.}}</ref>

Mingos' 1984 paper on the [[polyhedral skeletal electron pair theory]] develops [[Kenneth Wade|Wade's]] electron counting rules for predicting the [[molecular geometry]] of [[cluster compound]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Polyhedral Skeletal Electron Pair Approach|author=Mingos, D. M. P|journal=[[Acc. Chem. Res.]]|year=1984|volume=17|issue=9|pages=311–319|doi=10.1021/ar00105a003}}</ref>

In 1990 he was appointed [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] in Inorganic Chemistry and for the academic year 1991/92 he served as [[Assessor (Oxford)|Assessor]]. From 1992 until 1999 he worked at [[Imperial College London]] as [[Edward Frankland|Sir Edward Frankland]] [[BP]] Professor of Inorganic Chemistry (1992–99) and [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the [[Royal College of Science]] (1996–99).

In 1999 Mingos was appointed Principal of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oxford University Gazette, 29 April 1999: News Pages |url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/1998-9/weekly/290499/news/story_4.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170558/http://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/1998-9/weekly/290499/news/story_4.htm |archive-date=2016-03-03 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.ox.ac.uk}}</ref> and at the same time he became a visiting professor at [[Imperial College London]]. In 2000 he received as a [[Title of Distinction]] the title of professor of inorganic chemistry at the University of Oxford. He was superseded as principal by Professor [[Keith Gull]] on 1 October 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full History of the Hall |url=https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/about-college/full-history-hall |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714045647/https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/about-college/full-history-hall |archive-date=2018-07-14 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=St Edmund Hall |language=en}}</ref>

With [[David J. Wales]] he is the co-author of the textbook ''Introduction to Cluster Chemistry''.<ref name=clusterchem>{{cite book | last1 = Mingos | first1 = D. M. P. |last2 = Wales | first2 = D. J. |authorlink1=Michael Mingos|authorlink2=David J. Wales| title = Introduction to cluster chemistry | publisher = Prentice Hall | location = Englewood Cliffs, N.J | year = 1990 | isbn = 978-0134743059 }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 1980, Mingos was award the [[Corday-Morgan Medal]] and Prize of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]. He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1992|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1992]].

==Personal life==
Michael Mingos is the son of Vasso Mingos, of [[Athens]], and Rose Enid Billie Mingos ''née'' Griffiths.
